name: Tegla Loroupe
tagline: The barefoot girl who outran the world
story:
She grew up in a village in West Pokot, Kenya — one of 25 children, in a community where girls didn't run. Running was for boys. School was a luxury. Her father resisted her education; her community mocked her ambitions. But Tegla ran anyway, often barefoot, often hungry, covering miles of rough terrain just to get to school each morning.

In 1994, she lined up at the New York City Marathon as a relative unknown — a tiny Kenyan woman barely five feet tall in a field of giants. Nobody expected her to contend. She won. She broke the world marathon record. Then she broke it again. She became the first African woman to win a major marathon, shattering not just records but an entire edifice of assumptions about what women from her world could achieve.

But the running was never just about running. After retiring from competition, Tegla turned her fame into a weapon against conflict. In the war-torn border regions of Kenya, Uganda, and Sudan, she organized peace marathons — races where rival warriors from feuding tribes ran side by side instead of fighting. She convinced warlords to lay down arms, literally trading guns for running shoes. Her foundation has disarmed thousands.

When the IOC created the Refugee Olympic Team for the 2016 Rio Games, they chose Tegla Loroupe to lead it. The barefoot girl from West Pokot walked into the Olympic stadium carrying the hopes of 65 million displaced people. Some races you win with your legs. The ones that matter, you win with your heart.
